*Learn-the-tool track · Lab 3 of 3.*

Predictive uncertainty without posteriors.  Two questions, two tools: **predict the
noise** for the aleatoric part, **resample-and-refit** for the epistemic part.

---

## 1 · Aleatoric — Predict the Noise

When the noise level varies with `x`, one global error bar is wrong everywhere —
too wide where the world is calm, too narrow where it is loud.  Fit the mean, then
fit a *second* model to the **squared residuals** → a noise level `σ(x)`.

```{python}
x, y = datasets.heteroscedastic_noise(n=250, seed=0)
mu = np.polyval(np.polyfit(x, y, 5), x)        # mean model
resid = y - mu                                  # residuals = the noise
sigma = np.sqrt(np.clip(np.polyval(np.polyfit(x, resid**2, 2), x), 1e-6, None))
const = resid.std()

print(f"constant band : 2σ coverage {np.mean(np.abs(resid) <= 2 * const):.2f}")
print(f"σ(x) band     : 2σ coverage {np.mean(np.abs(resid) <= 2 * sigma):.2f}")
print(f"σ(x) ranges {sigma.min():.2f} (calm)  ..  {sigma.max():.2f} (noisy)")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-tool3-aleatoric
#| fig-cap: "Constant error bar (left) vs predicted sigma(x) (right). Both reach ~95% coverage, but only sigma(x) puts the band where the noise actually is."
fig, (axL, axR) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 3.8), sharey=True)
axL.fill_between(x, mu - 2 * const, mu + 2 * const, color=CRASH, alpha=0.18)
axL.scatter(x, y, s=12, c=INK, alpha=0.6); axL.plot(x, mu, c=INK, lw=2)
axL.set_title("constant noise — one bar", fontsize=12); despine(axL)
axR.fill_between(x, mu - 2 * sigma, mu + 2 * sigma, color=COOL, alpha=0.30)
axR.scatter(x, y, s=12, c=INK, alpha=0.6); axR.plot(x, mu, c=INK, lw=2)
axR.set_title("predicted σ(x) — breathes", fontsize=12); despine(axR)
for ax in (axL, axR):
    ax.set_xlabel("x"); ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([])
axL.set_ylabel("y")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## 2 · Epistemic — Ensemble of Refits

A different question — *has the model seen data here?* — needs a different tool.
Refit on bootstrap resamples; the members' spread is the epistemic band.

```{python}
xg, yg = datasets.heteroscedastic_gap(n=60, seed=0)
xs = np.linspace(-5, 5, 300)
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
ens = np.array([
    np.polyval(np.polyfit(xg[i], yg[i], 5), xs)
    for i in (rng.integers(0, xg.size, xg.size) for _ in range(40))
])
e_mean, e_sd = ens.mean(0), ens.std(0)
gap = (xs > -1) & (xs < 1)
print(f"epistemic sd in data  : {e_sd[~gap & (np.abs(xs) < 3)].mean():.2f}")
print(f"epistemic sd in gap   : {e_sd[gap].mean():.2f}   ← wider where data is sparse")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-tool3-epistemic
#| fig-cap: "Ensemble spread is tight where data is dense and balloons over the gap and the extrapolation edges."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 3.8))
ax.fill_between(xs, e_mean - 2 * e_sd, e_mean + 2 * e_sd,
                color=plotting.PALETTE["green"], alpha=0.25)
for member in ens[:12]:
    ax.plot(xs, member, c=plotting.PALETTE["green"], lw=0.6, alpha=0.4)
ax.plot(xs, e_mean, c=INK, lw=2); ax.scatter(xg, yg, s=18, c=INK, zorder=5)
ax.axvspan(-1, 1, color=CRASH, alpha=0.06)
ax.set_ylim(-2.2, 2.2); ax.set_xlabel("x"); ax.set_ylabel("y")
ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([]); despine(ax)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## What to Look for
The two bands answer different questions.  **Aleatoric** `σ(x)` follows the noise
and *will not* shrink with more data.  **Epistemic** spread collapses where data is
dense and balloons where you have none — add data and it shrinks.  The honest total
is `σ²(x) = σ²_aleatoric(x) + σ²_epistemic(x)`.
:::
